sources.citation: ms.wikipedia.org 'Bahasa Melayu Cheti' (wikitext, downloaded 2026-09-17), phonology section sourced to Mohamed 2009 JMBRAS pp.60-65

sources.note: Secondary. Lists only segmental features from the JMBRAS article (final /r/ and /h/ deletion, ai>e, au>o, mb>m, final glottal insertion); nothing on stress or intonation.

sources.citation: Paauw, Scott H. 2009. The Malay contact varieties of eastern Indonesia: A typological comparison. PhD dissertation, SUNY Buffalo. xxiii+717 pp. (Glottolog ref 124406.)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Single mention (PDF p.48, sec. 2.2.1.1): Malaysian Bazaar Malay 'spoken by Indians is sometimes called Chitty Malay.. Three short studies do not provide a great deal of descriptive information'. No phonology of Chitty Malay.

sources.citation: Noriah Mohamed & Meriam Abd. Karim. 2005. Penggunaan Bahasa Melayu Kreol Chetti Melaka: Satu Analisis Domain. Jurnal Bahasa (DBP) 5(1): 1-50. USM eprints 10531.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Open scan (29 pp., no text layer; scanned to). Fishman-domain language-choice survey of 60-odd Chetti informants; nothing on phonology or stress. Footnote states it stems from the USM project 'Deskripsi Leksiko-Fonologi Bahasa Kreol Melayu Chetti Melaka' (April 2004 - May 2006).

sources.citation: Lim, Sonny. 1988. Baba Malay: the language of the 'Straits-born' Chinese. Papers in Western Austronesian Linguistics 3, 1-61. Pacific Linguistics A-78.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Chitty-Indian Malay speech samples recorded for syntactic comparison (p.2; sec. 5.1 pp.49-50 and fn. 6: Chitty-Malay shares Baba Malay's punya constructions etc.). Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Lee, Nala H. 2022. A Grammar of Modern Baba Malay. De Gruyter Mouton (ch. 3 Phonetics and phonology; ch. 6 on Singapore vs Malacca Baba Malay).

sources.note: Closest described sister creole (final-syllable stress per Lee 2014); check whether it comments on Chetti Malay prosody when discussing Malacca varieties.
